physical_harm: Injuries were caused, but the specific nature of injuries is not detailed
number_of_offences: Two offences were charged and both were upheld
premeditation_planning: The court found that the accused had planned to deceive the prosecutrix by promising marriage
motive: The motive was to deceive the prosecutrix and engage in sexual intercourse under the pretense of marriage
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted the statements of the prosecutrix (PW1), her brother (PW2), her father (PW4), and the village elders (PWs5, 6, 7, and 8), along with the friends of the accused (PWs9 and 10), as credible evidence of the accused's deceitful actions and the non-consensual sexual relationship.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the main witnesses as credible, noting that their statements, when examined in conjunction, left no room for doubt regarding the accused's deceitful actions and the non-consensual nature of the sexual relationship.
post_offence_conduct: The accused surrendered to the Judicial Magistrate on 5.11.2003.
bail_history: Accused-appellant Karthick was ordered to be released on bail by this Court vide order dated 4.4.2008. He shall now be taken into custody, to serve the remaining part of the sentence.
trial_duration: The accusation was made on 10.10.2003. The accused-appellant surrendered before the Judicial Magistrate on 5.11.2003. The trial court convicted the appellant under Sections 376 and 417 IPC. The conviction was affirmed by the appellate Court and the Revisional Court. The appeal was dismissed by the Supreme Court.
legal_representation: R. Balasubrmanian, K.V. Vijayakumar, T.R.B. Siva Kumar for the Appellant. A. Yogesh Kanna, A. Santha Kumaran, B. Balaji for the Respondent.
investigation_status: A charge-sheet was filed before the Judicial Magistrate No.II, Virudhunagar. The matter was committed to the Principal District and Sessions Court, Virudhunagar at Srivilliputtur.
appeal_history: The trial court convicted the appellant under Sections 376 and 417 IPC. The conviction was affirmed by the appellate Court and the Revisional Court. The appeal was dismissed by the Supreme Court.
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the accused-appellant committed deceit with PW1 by promising to marry her, leading to an unwilling sexual relationship. The accused forced himself on PW1 after gagging her mouth, and subsequent acts of sexual intercourse were actions of actively cheating her by giving her the impression that he would marry her. The delay in FIR registration did not affect the prosecution's version.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the accused-appellant did not commit rape as the sexual intercourse was consensual, and that the delay in FIR registration raised doubts about the prosecution's story. They also relied on precedents suggesting that consent obtained through a promise of marriage may not be considered a misconception of fact.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that obtaining consent by exercising deceit cannot be a legitimate defence to exculpate an accused. The Court emphasized that the burden of proof lies with the prosecution to establish the absence of consent.
precedent_relied_upon: Uday v. State of Karnataka (2003) 4 SCC 46; Zinder Ali Sheikh vs. State of West Bengal & Anr. (2009) 3 SCC 761
sentencing_rationale: The final sentence was imposed because the accused-appellant committed deceit with PW1 by promising to marry her, leading to an unwilling sexual relationship. The Court found that the sexual intercourse was not consensual and that the accused had actively cheated PW1.
